seo.title: How to Claim Your Google Business Profile (2026)
seo.meta_description: How to claim an existing Google Business Profile for an Anaheim or Orange County business: unverified profiles, ownership requests and verification.

h1: How to Claim Your Google Business Profile on Google Maps
answer: To claim your Google Business Profile, find your business on Google Maps, select Claim this business and then Manage now, and complete a verification option. It is free. If someone else has already verified the profile, you request ownership from the current owner instead. Many Anaheim and Orange County businesses already have an unclaimed profile built from public information.
key_takeaways: Unclaimed profiles can be claimed from Google Maps.
Verified profiles need an ownership request.

sections.heading: Why your business may already be on Google
sections.body_html: Google builds many listings from public information, so your business may appear on Maps before you ever touch it. Until you claim and verify it, you cannot control what it says. Wrong hours or an old phone number on an unclaimed profile cost calls every day.

sections.heading: Claiming is free
sections.body_html: Google's help page says you can add or claim your business at no charge. Be wary of anyone who calls offering to claim or verify your listing for a fee or asking for your verification code.

sections.heading: Claim on a computer
sections.body_html: Open Google Maps, search for your business name and city, or find it on the map, and select it. Select Claim this business, then Manage now. If the business shown is not yours, choose I own or manage another business. Select a verification option and follow the instructions.

sections.heading: Claim in the Google Maps app
sections.body_html: Open the Google Maps app, search for the business name and select the correct result. In the profile, tap About, then Claim this business and Manage now. Choose a verification option and follow the steps.

sections.heading: If someone else verified it
sections.body_html: Google says that if a profile has been verified and you are authorized to manage the business, you can request ownership from the current owner. This often happens when a former employee, agency or previous owner set up the profile. Keep records showing you own or manage the business.

sections.heading: Check eligibility first
sections.body_html: Only businesses eligible for a Business Profile can claim one: businesses that meet customers in person at a location or by visiting them. Make sure the address shown is one you actually operate from, or switch to a service area if you visit customers.

sections.heading: Avoid duplicates
sections.body_html: If you find two listings for your business, do not create a third. Claim the correct one and use Google's help for duplicate profiles and ownership issues. Duplicates split reviews and confuse customers.

sections.heading: After claiming: fix everything
sections.body_html: Once verified, correct the name, category, hours, phone and website, add services and photos, and reply to existing reviews. Old reviews on an unclaimed profile often went unanswered for years.

sections.heading: Who should own the profile
sections.body_html: Use a Google Account the business controls. Add staff or agencies as managers rather than sharing passwords, so access can be removed when people leave.

sections.heading: Claiming and AI search
sections.body_html: AI assistants and Google's AI features draw on business listings. A claimed, accurate profile is one of the clearest signals about your business, so claiming it helps them describe you correctly.

sections.heading: Checklist
sections.body_html:
• Found the correct listing on Maps.
  • Selected Claim this business, then Manage now.
  • Completed verification.
  • Requested ownership if someone else verified it.
  • Corrected name, hours, phone and website.
  • Replied to old reviews.
  • Added managers instead of sharing passwords.

sections.heading: Common problems when claiming
sections.body_html:
• The claim button is missing because the profile is already verified by someone else; request ownership instead.
  • A former agency or employee owns the profile and has stopped responding; keep records and use Google's ownership request route.
  • There are two listings for the same business; claim the right one and deal with the duplicate rather than adding another.
  • The address on the listing is an old location; correct it after claiming, before you start verification if possible.
  • Someone calls offering to claim or verify the listing for a fee; claiming is free, so decline.

sections.heading: Questions to answer before you claim
sections.body_html: Before you start, confirm three things. First, that the listing really is your business and not a similarly named one in another Orange County city. Second, which Google Account should own it: ideally one the business controls, not a personal account belonging to one person. Third, whether customers visit you or you visit them, because that decides whether the profile shows an address or a service area. Answering these up front avoids the most common clean-up jobs later. Once the profile is yours, keep a short note of who owns it, who manages it and when access was last reviewed, so the business never has to recover its own listing again.

sections.heading: An example
sections.body_html: Imagine a family restaurant in Garden Grove that has been open for 15 years but never claimed its profile. The listing shows old hours and a disconnected phone number. The owner searches Maps, selects Claim this business, verifies by phone, then fixes the hours and number, adds the menu link and replies to years of unanswered reviews. A manager account is added for the general manager.

sections.heading: How this fits your local plan
sections.body_html: Treat this as part of a routine rather than a one-off fix. Local visibility in Anaheim and the rest of Orange County comes from many small, accurate signals adding up: a verified profile, consistent listings, useful service pages, real photos and a flow of honest reviews. Google is open that relevance, distance and popularity drive local results. You cannot change distance, but you can make sure Google and AI assistants understand exactly what you do and see evidence that customers value it. Put a monthly reminder in the calendar to check the profile, read new reviews and update anything that has changed.

sections.heading: Questions owners ask us
sections.body_html: Owners often ask whether claiming will erase the reviews already on the listing. It does not: reviews stay with the profile, which is one reason to claim the existing listing rather than start again. Another common question is whether a claimed listing will rank immediately. Claiming gives you control; rankings improve as you complete the profile, earn reviews and keep details accurate. Owners also ask what happens if verification fails. Check that the name, address and category follow Google's guidelines, fix anything that does not, and try again with the methods Google offers.

sections.heading: What to do this week
sections.body_html:
1. Search Maps for your business.
  2. Claim it or request ownership.
  3. Verify.
  4. Correct every detail and reply to old reviews.

sections.heading: When to get help
sections.body_html: You do not need an agency for every step here; Google documents most of it clearly. Consider outside help when the work is urgent and unfamiliar, when you manage several locations, or when the same issue returns after you fix it. Ask any provider to show you the specific guideline or documentation behind each recommendation, to keep you as the owner of your accounts and to report results in calls, bookings and leads rather than vanity numbers. That is how Chimera works with Orange County businesses from our base in Anaheim.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Find your business on Maps, select Claim this business, verify, then fix every detail. If someone else owns it, request ownership. Chimera, based in Anaheim, helps Orange County businesses recover and clean up profiles.

faqs.q: How do I claim my business on Google?
faqs.a: Find it on Google Maps, select Claim this business, then Manage now, and verify.

faqs.q: Is claiming a Google Business Profile free?
faqs.a: Yes. Google says you can add or claim your business at no charge.

faqs.q: What if someone else already verified my profile?
faqs.a: If you're authorized, request ownership from the current profile owner.

faqs.q: Can I claim from the Google Maps app?
faqs.a: Yes. Open the profile, tap About, then Claim this business.

faqs.q: Should I create a new profile instead?
faqs.a: No. Claim the existing one to avoid duplicates.
A Google Account the business controls, with others added as managers.
